title: No session log books
summary: Matassa has only old appointment books and Disc Masters logs in storage; sessions were often logged just by label or bandleader, and he was not organized.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

No. The only log I've got, I've got some of my old appointment books, and I've got the master logs from when I was doing Disc Masters.
I've got them somewhere in storage. I've got a thing over in Fidel. I've got a bunch of junk in storage. I've got to get that stuff out and go through it.
You ought to sometime. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. But you don't think you'd have any books from 1949, 50?
I don't know what years they are. I don't know what years they are.
To know, hey, this session, this session, this session.
No, I'd have to. Well, a lot of times, it wouldn't even say it. It'd just say Imperial or David Tholomew or something like that. You know, it was very...
You weren't much of a bookkeeper?

Do you really think you didn't capitalize on...
